analysis:
The changes are documentation only. They cover docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (lines 298-299, 338-358) and docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 404-410, 1050-1070). I found no executable code, wire protocol, attestation, authorization or key-handling change in the supplied evidence. The documented behavior is as follows.

(1) Load gates, including Nemotron Super, release retained free KV segments and drop the MLX buffer cache before evicting. Pre-accept counts retained segments as reachable.
(2) Segmented paged pools park released free 64 MiB segments, up to min(2 GiB, grant/8), outside the grant, floor and ledger charge. The next same-size admission reinstalls them.
(3) Parked segments are dropped on refused admission, on a process-wide release request, and after 30 s idle.
(4) New segments use zero-fill-on-demand host pages.
(5) The idle allocator-cache sweep now runs through WholeMacServiceBudget.performIfIdle after 5 s of idleness. Two env switches restore the old behavior.

Threat-model relevance: this is memory and availability accounting (TB-007; T-010, T-029) and residual in-memory inference data (T-028). The provider operator is already the adversary for process memory (T-011, T-014). Parked segments keep KV bytes derived from prior requests resident in the provider process for up to 30 s longer. That is within the existing T-028 posture. The parked backing is documented as uncharged, but the same text says load admission counts it as reclaimable, so I see no concrete regression from the docs alone.

Open questions for code reviewers (the source was not supplied): whether the reinstall path leaks prior-request KV into a new request's readable region, which is a correctness concern, not a consumer-facing disclosure. Also whether uncharged parked memory (at most 2 GiB) can cause OOM under pressure. Also whether the release-on-pressure triggers behave as documented. Neither the prefix-cache SSD tier (T-041) nor any coordinator/provider boundary is touched. Nothing here changes the trust-boundary contracts, so no finding qualifies.
